bifrost: none in the SDK or shell. Nearest code: springboard/apps/keyboard/src/predict.rs (prefix trie and bigram counts, not a learned model), springboard/sdk/src/spellcheck.rs (word checks, no model)
summary: Core ML runs trained models on the device (MLModel, feature providers, tensors, compute-device policy, on-device updates). BifrOSt has no model loading, inference, tensor or feature-provider API, and no SDK module for it. The keyboard predictor is a hand-built word-frequency trie, and the Assistant app calls a remote Messages API, so neither is an on-device model.

features.note: verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 7 tests. Wave 3 (w3-core-ml, parity/integration cf8e852d): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. no SDK API loads a compiled model or runs a prediction Built 2026-10-17: bifrost_app::core_ml re-exports Model, AnalysisRuntime and the feature provider types for apps, so an app can load a model and run a prediction in the SDK (sdk/src/core_ml.rs, tests core_ml::tests). Wiring into a shell app is still open.

gaps: No SDK API to load a model file and run a prediction (MLModel, MLFeatureProvider)
No tensor or numeric array type for model inputs and outputs (MLTensor, MLFeatureValue)
No compute-device policy exposed to apps (CPU, GPU, Neural Engine); the GPU is used only for rendering
No domain APIs on top of inference: image classification, speech, sound analysis, natural language
No model encryption, runtime model download and compile, or on-device update path
The on-device keyboard predictor is not a learned model; the Assistant app uses a remote API, which is not Core ML
